---
title: "Outputs, analysis, and restart"
---

## Run directory {#sec-run-directory}

Every run gets its own explicit `--output` directory. The facade writes
metadata before starting the child and updates completion/failure status when
the process exits.
{{< src "src/provenance.jl" "function run_simulation" >}}

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `metadata.toml` | Input configuration, source fingerprint, Julia/system details, manifest hash, status, wall time |
| `Project.toml`, `Manifest.toml` | Copies of the active environment declarations/manifest when present |
| `resolved-environment.toml` | All facade-resolved solver options and output paths |
| `run.log` | Solver stdout/stderr, stage timings, warnings, diagnostic summaries |
| `history.tsv` | Small redshift/time histories |
| `spectra.tsv` | Shell/angle power tables with explicit field labels and mode counts |
| `pdfs.tsv` | Gas/DM density histograms |
| `modes.tsv` | Matched-mode Fourier diagnostics where enabled |
| `performance.tsv` | Run-level phase averages and model/initialization metadata |
| `checkpoint.jls` | Restart state, only when checkpoint writing is enabled |

Files can be absent when their diagnostic is disabled or a run fails before
its first output. A path in the resolved configuration does not prove a file
was written. Check `metadata.toml`, the log, and the final achieved redshift.

`COMPLETED` means the requested trajectory reached its target. A cosmological
run that exits successfully at a cycle budget before `zend` is
`STOPPED_AT_LIMIT`, not completed science. `INCOMPLETE` denotes a missing final
redshift record; `FAILED` denotes an execution error. Do not treat exit code
zero or a final diagnostic file alone as proof the endpoint was reached.
{{< src "src/provenance.jl" "function _completion_status" >}}

## Histories and cadence {#sec-histories}

`history.tsv` includes `cycle`, `measured`, `z`, `a`, `brms`,
`divBdx_over_brms`, `delta_b_rms`, `delta_dm_rms`, mean/min/max abundances,
`xe_total`, transverse-mode diagnostics, pressure, internal energy, and
temperature statistics. `brms` is in **code units**, temperature is K, and
disabled physical channels may appear as `NaN`; do not substitute zero.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _write_history!" >}}

`diagnostics.redshifts` requests common comparison epochs;
`diagnostics.every` sets a cycle cadence. Adaptive histories can add samples
where density/ionization changes. Initial spectra require `MHD_INITIAL_PK=1`
(enabled by the facade); final diagnostics are enabled by default. Use the
actual `z` column for alignment rather than assuming the same cycle means the
same physical epoch.

## Power spectra {#sec-power-spectra}

The shared TSV schema is

```text
field cycle measured z a kbin mubin k mu_lo mu_hi P Nmodes
```

`Nmodes=0` bins are empty, not zero power measurements. Gas/DM density,
magnetic vector, photon density, and magnetic force spectra use one isotropic
mu bin. Photon velocity and photon-baryon slip can retain angular bins.
Vector power sums components; it is not a single-component spectrum.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _write_pkmu!" >}}
{{< src "lib/PoissonKernels/src/gpu_fft.jl" "power_spectrum_aniso_gpu" >}}

`B_pressure_force`, `B_tension_force`, and `B_lorentz_force` use the Maxwell
split in @eq-maxwell. Recover their cross spectrum using

$$
2P_{PT}=P_L-P_P-P_T.
$$ {#eq-cross-spectrum}

Changing cancellation between pressure and tension can alter total force
power even when each auto-spectrum changes little. Density/particle mesh
spectra are estimator outputs: do not presume a shot-noise subtraction or
CIC-window deconvolution that is not explicitly performed by the implementation.
Fix `MHD_PK_KMAX` and bin counts across grids for common physical edges.

The numeric `k` follows `MHD_BOXSIZE`, which defaults to **1**. The physical
TOML box does not by itself change that diagnostic option. Convert the axes
and volume normalization using [notation](notation.qmd#sec-wavenumbers).

## PDFs and images {#sec-plots}

The density PDF is per unit `log10(rho)` with normalization by total grid
cells and bin width. Its schema includes `field`, epoch, bin edges,
`rho_mid`, `count`, and `pdf`. Check histogram support before interpreting tails;
do not compare a log-density PDF directly to a PDF per unit linear density.

Optional `MHD_DENSITY_FRAME_DIR` and `MHD_DENSITY_FRAME_ZS` request density
frames. `MHD_FINAL_B_DIR` writes a final magnetic-field payload. These are
separate from the small summary tables and can add substantial transfers and
storage. The Python tools under `tools/analysis` consume the actual TSV schemas;
their command-line help and `tools/README.md` describe supported plots.

```sh
uv sync --extra test
# A cosmological run can infer units from its metadata:
uv run pmf-analyze results/cosmology-first
# Explicit physical units and a separate output directory:
uv run pmf-analyze results/first --output results/first-analysis \
  --length-unit box \
  --box-ckpc-h 1 --spectral-boxsize 1 --hubble 0.674
```

With a run-directory argument, tables are discovered automatically and the
default plot directory is `RUN_DIR/analysis`. Metadata supplies units for a
cosmological run when available; explicit flags override inference. The unit
flags in the second command explicitly assign a 1 ckpc/h physical box to the otherwise
dimensionless smoke case; replace them with the actual experiment's values.
For the cosmological example, use its configured `box_ckpc_h`, `h`, and any
`MHD_BOXSIZE` override. The command writes PDF/PNG diagnostics and an input-hash
record; it does not convert code magnetic/force amplitudes into cgs silently.

For optional density frames:

```sh
uv run python -m tools.analysis.render_density_frames path/to/frames \
  results/frame-plots --box-ckpc-h 1 --hubble 0.674 --log-min -2 --log-max 2
```

The two panels are a central density slice and a line-of-sight **maximum**, not
an integrated column density. Fixed color limits support epoch-to-epoch
comparison; supplied physical box units label axes in comoving kpc without h.

With FFmpeg installed separately, combine the cycle-sorted PNGs into a movie:

```sh
ffmpeg -framerate 12 -pattern_type glob -i 'results/frame-plots/density_cycle*.png' \
  -vf 'scale=1440:640:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1440:640:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2' \
  -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p results/density-evolution.mp4
```

Keep the same log-density color limits for every frame and comparison run.
The fixed output dimensions also avoid small caption/bounding-box differences
changing the encoded frame size. Archive `frames.json` and the original tables
with the movie so its epochs and color normalization remain recoverable.

Keep raw tables alongside generated figures. Plot captions should state the
field, actual redshift, physical units, band/window, normalization, and whether
the plotted quantity is `P(k)` or dimensionless `k^3 P/(2*pi^2)`.

## Checkpoints and restart {#sec-restart}

Enable checkpointing in the original configuration:

```toml
[run]
checkpoint_every = 100
checkpoint_final = true
resume = false
```

To continue, change `resume=true`, preserve all evolution settings, and rerun
against the same output directory. Extending `cosmology.zend` is allowed by
the driver; changing its physical history is not generally compatible.
The wrapper additionally rejects a changed source fingerprint.

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl path/to/resume.toml \
  --backend=cpu --output=results/my-run
```

The checkpoint writer streams fields through host arrays to a temporary file,
then renames it. It stores configuration, runtime counters/clocks, MHD fields,
particle and chemistry state, and active photon/compensation payloads. Restore
checks field ordering, shape, type, and configuration compatibility.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _write_pmf_checkpoint" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _restore_pmf_checkpoint!" >}}

Julia Serialization is a restart mechanism, **not** a long-term portable
archive or an untrusted-file format. Keep the Julia version, manifest, source,
and metadata with a checkpoint; never deserialize untrusted files. The code's
legacy/override migration paths are expert operations, not a promise of
cross-version or cross-backend portability.

Restart logs/tables can append to earlier outputs. Check for repeated epochs
and preserve pre-resume metadata when publishing an audit trail. Validate a
continuous versus split/resumed trajectory before relying on a new checkpoint
configuration.
